citations.claim: "Danger" correct for Flam. Liq. 2
citations.evidence: App. C table C.4.19 Flammable Liquids: category 2 — signal word "Danger", hazard statement "Highly flammable liquid and vapor" (category 3 is "Flammable liquid and vapor"), flame pictogram.

citations.claim: product identifier present; must match SDS
citations.evidence: (c): "Product identifier means the name or number used for a hazardous chemical on a label or in the SDS ... The product identifier used shall permit cross-references to be made among the list of hazardous chemicals ..., the label and the SDS."; App. D Table D.1 Section 1(a): "Product identifier used on the label"; (g)(2) requires the SDS sections per Appendix D.

citations.claim: supplier name and address present
citations.evidence: (f)(1)(vi) "Name, U.S. address, and U.S. telephone number of the chemical manufacturer, importer, or other responsible party."

citations.claim: each container leaving the workplace must carry all elements; pointer to carton does not satisfy
citations.evidence: (f)(1): "each container of hazardous chemicals leaving the workplace is labeled, tagged or marked ... the following shall be provided: (i) Product identifier; (ii) Signal word; (iii) Hazard statement(s); (iv) Pictogram(s); (v) Precautionary statement(s); (vi) Name, U.S. address, and U.S. telephone number of the chemical manufacturer, importer, or other responsible party." (but see (f)(12) — the answer ignores it)

citations.claim: hazard statement H225 "Highly flammable liquid and vapor"
citations.evidence: (f)(1)(iii) "Hazard statement(s);"; App. C table C.4.19 Flammable Liquids: category 2 — signal word "Danger", hazard statement "Highly flammable liquid and vapor" (category 3 is "Flammable liquid and vapor"), flame pictogram.

citations.claim: precautionary statements required
citations.evidence: (f)(1)(v) "Precautionary statement(s);"; Table C.4.19 lists for flammable liquids: "Keep away from heat, hot surfaces, sparks, open flames and other ignition sources. No smoking."; "Keep container tightly closed."; "Ground and bond container and receiving equipment."; "Use explosion-proof [electrical/ventilating/lighting/...] equipment."; "Use non-sparking tools."; "Take action to prevent static discharge."; "Wear protective gloves/protective clothing/eye protection..."; "If on skin (or hair): Take off immediately all contaminated clothing. Rinse skin with water [or shower]."; "In case of fire: Use ... to extinguish."; "Store in a well-ventilated place. Keep cool."; "Dispose of contents/container to..." (OSHA prints no P-codes, but the GHS codes listed map to these statements).

citations.claim: telephone number required
citations.evidence: (f)(1)(vi) "Name, U.S. address, and U.S. telephone number of the chemical manufacturer, importer, or other responsible party." The small-container equivalent is (f)(12)(ii)(D) "Chemical manufacturer's name and phone number".

citations.claim: black symbol, white background, red diamond border; no minimum size
citations.evidence: (f)(1)(iv) "Pictogram(s);"; App. C.2.3.1: "Pictograms shall be in the shape of a square set at a point and shall include a black hazard symbol on a white background with a red frame sufficiently wide to be clearly visible."; No minimum pictogram size exists anywhere in 1910.1200 (no "cm"/"mm" figure for pictograms); (f)(1)(iv) reads only "Pictogram(s);" and C.2.3.1 sets only shape and colour.

citations.claim: label identifier, classification and hazard statements must agree with SDS
citations.evidence: App. D Table D.1, Section 2(b): "Signal word, hazard statement(s), symbol(s) and precautionary statement(s) in accordance with paragraph (f) of §1910.1200"; App. D intro: "Sections 12-15 may be included in the SDS, but are not mandatory" (Section 15 adds nothing).

citations.claim: DOT applies separately
citations.evidence: Not among the provided sources (49 CFR not fetched); (f)(5)(i) only confirms HazCom labels must not conflict with DOT rules.

citations.claim: consumer sales fall under FHSA instead
citations.evidence: FHSA / 16 CFR 1500 not among sources; not verified. (OSHA (b)(5)(v) does carve CPSA/FHSA-labelled products out of HazCom labeling.)

otherClaims.claim: OSHA has no reduced small-container label provision
otherClaims.quote: (f)(12)(i): "This paragraph applies where the chemical manufacturer, importer, or distributor can demonstrate that it is not feasible to use pull-out labels, fold-back labels, or tags containing the full label information required by paragraph (f)(1)"; (f)(12)(ii): "For a container less than or equal to 100 ml capacity, the chemical manufacturer, importer, or distributor must include, at a minimum, the following information on the label of the container: (A) Product identifier; (B) Pictogram(s); (C) Signal word; (D) Chemical manufacturer's name and phone number; and (E) A statement that the full label information for the hazardous chemical is provided on the immediate outer package."

answers.notes: Caught the missing phone number, but via the general (f)(1)(vi) on the false premise that OSHA has no small-container provision. Hazard/precautionary claims are only right if the (f)(12)(i) infeasibility condition is not met — facts not given, so unclear.

citations.claim: all six elements required on each shipped container
citations.evidence: (f)(1): "each container of hazardous chemicals leaving the workplace is labeled, tagged or marked ... the following shall be provided: (i) Product identifier; (ii) Signal word; (iii) Hazard statement(s); (iv) Pictogram(s); (v) Precautionary statement(s); (vi) Name, U.S. address, and U.S. telephone number of the chemical manufacturer, importer, or other responsible party."

citations.claim: reduced-content labels exist under CLP
citations.evidence: CLP (consolidated 2026-07-01) Art. 29 "Exemptions from labelling and packaging requirements": "(2) If the full label information cannot be provided in the way specified in paragraph 1 the label information may be reduced in accordance with section 1.5.2 of Annex I."

citations.claim: label is information on the immediate container, so a carton label does not satisfy
citations.evidence: (c): "Label means an appropriate group of written, printed or graphic information elements concerning a hazardous chemical that is affixed to, printed on, or attached to the immediate container of a hazardous chemical, or to the outside packaging." — the definition expressly includes the outside packaging.

citations.claim: the "full label on outer package" sentence is not required, only allowed as supplementary information
citations.evidence: App. C.3.1-C.3.2 govern optional supplementary information; but (f)(12)(ii)(E) makes "A statement that the full label information for the hazardous chemical is provided on the immediate outer package" a required element of a small-container label.

citations.claim: black symbol on white inside red diamond border, border clearly visible
citations.evidence: App. C.2.3.1: "Pictograms shall be in the shape of a square set at a point and shall include a black hazard symbol on a white background with a red frame sufficiently wide to be clearly visible."

citations.claim: product identifier must match SDS
citations.evidence: (f)(2): information under (f)(1)(i)-(v) shall be "in accordance with Appendix C ..., for each hazard class and associated hazard category ..., prominently displayed, and in English (other languages may also be included if appropriate)." — says nothing about matching the SDS; that is the (c) product-identifier definition / App. D Section 1(a).

citations.claim: label must reflect all classified hazards
citations.evidence: App. C.2: "The label for each hazardous chemical that is classified shall include the signal word, hazard statement(s), pictogram(s), and precautionary statement(s) specified in C.4 for each hazard class and associated hazard category"

citations.claim: English, prominently displayed, legible and durable
citations.evidence: (f)(10) is the employer's duty for workplace labels ("The employer shall ensure that workplace labels or other forms of warning are legible, in English, and prominently displayed"); for shipped containers English/prominence sits in (f)(2). Neither paragraph mentions durability.

citations.claim: consumer product may be outside HazCom
citations.evidence: (b)(6)(ix) exempts consumer products "where the employer can show that it is used in the workplace for the purpose intended ... and the use results in a duration and frequency of exposure which is not greater than ... consumers" — an employer-use exemption. The labeling carve-out is (b)(5)(v): "This section does not require labeling of ... Any consumer product or hazardous substance as those terms are defined in the Consumer Product Safety Act ... and Federal Hazardous Substances Act ..., when subject to a consumer product safety standard or labeling requirement of those Acts".

otherClaims.claim: OSHA did not adopt a reduced small-container label
otherClaims.quote: (f)(12)(i): "This paragraph applies where the chemical manufacturer, importer, or distributor can demonstrate that it is not feasible to use pull-out labels, fold-back labels, or tags containing the full label information required by paragraph (f)(1)"; (f)(12)(ii): "For a container less than or equal to 100 ml capacity, the chemical manufacturer, importer, or distributor must include, at a minimum, the following information on the label of the container: (A) Product identifier; (B) Pictogram(s); (C) Signal word; (D) Chemical manufacturer's name and phone number; and (E) A statement that the full label information for the hazardous chemical is provided on the immediate outer package."
(f)(12)(ii)(E): "A statement that the full label information for the hazardous chemical is provided on the immediate outer package."

answers.notes: Caught the missing phone number. Misreads the (c) Label definition, which expressly includes "the outside packaging", and calls the (f)(12)(ii)(E) statement optional.

citations.claim: product identifier must be consistent between small container and outer label
citations.evidence: (f)(1): "each container of hazardous chemicals leaving the workplace is labeled, tagged or marked ... the following shall be provided: (i) Product identifier; (ii) Signal word; (iii) Hazard statement(s); (iv) Pictogram(s); (v) Precautionary statement(s); (vi) Name, U.S. address, and U.S. telephone number of the chemical manufacturer, importer, or other responsible party." — no consistency rule; cross-referencing is in the (c) product identifier definition.

citations.claim: permits reduced labels on small containers if full information is on the outer package
citations.evidence: (f)(6) is "Workplace labeling" — the employer labels workplace containers with "(i) The information specified under paragraphs (f)(1)(i) through (v) ...; or, (ii) Product identifier and words, pictures, symbols ..." It has only (i) and (ii), and contains no size, small-container or reduced-label provision. The small-container rule is (f)(12).

citations.claim: "recommends" reduced labels include enough information for hazard recognition
citations.evidence: (f)(1): "each container of hazardous chemicals leaving the workplace is labeled, tagged or marked ... the following shall be provided: (i) Product identifier; (ii) Signal word; (iii) Hazard statement(s); (iv) Pictogram(s); (v) Precautionary statement(s); (vi) Name, U.S. address, and U.S. telephone number of the chemical manufacturer, importer, or other responsible party." — contains no such recommendation.

citations.claim: smaller pictograms allowed for small containers, not below ~6 mm
citations.evidence: (f)(6) has only paragraphs (i) and (ii); there is no (f)(6)(iii). No minimum pictogram size exists anywhere in 1910.1200 (no "cm"/"mm" figure for pictograms); (f)(1)(iv) reads only "Pictogram(s);" and C.2.3.1 sets only shape and colour.

otherClaims.quote: Label prints "Example solvent"; (f)(12)(ii)(A) requires only "Product identifier".

otherClaims.claim: pictogram must not fall below ~6 mm

answers.notes: Declares the label "largely compliant for a reduced small-container label" and misses the phone number. Invents (f)(6)(iii) and a 6 mm figure.

citations.claim: labels must include hazard statements
citations.evidence: (f)(1)(vi) "Name, U.S. address, and U.S. telephone number of the chemical manufacturer, importer, or other responsible party." Hazard statements are (f)(1)(iii).

citations.claim: allows reduced small-container labelling but hazard statements must still appear on the small container
citations.evidence: (f)(2): information under (f)(1)(i)-(v) shall be "in accordance with Appendix C ..., for each hazard class and associated hazard category ..., prominently displayed, and in English (other languages may also be included if appropriate)." The small-container rule is (f)(12)(ii), which does not list hazard statements: (f)(12)(i): "This paragraph applies where the chemical manufacturer, importer, or distributor can demonstrate that it is not feasible to use pull-out labels, fold-back labels, or tags containing the full label information required by paragraph (f)(1)"; (f)(12)(ii): "For a container less than or equal to 100 ml capacity, the chemical manufacturer, importer, or distributor must include, at a minimum, the following information on the label of the container: (A) Product identifier; (B) Pictogram(s); (C) Signal word; (D) Chemical manufacturer's name and phone number; and (E) A statement that the full label information for the hazardous chemical is provided on the immediate outer package."

It has only (i) and (ii), and contains no size, small-container or reduced-label provision. No minimum pictogram size exists anywhere in 1910.1200 (no "cm"/"mm" figure for pictograms); (f)(1)(iv) reads only "Pictogram(s);" and C.2.3.1 sets only shape and colour.

otherClaims.claim: precautionary statements required on small-container label
otherClaims.quote: (f)(12)(i): "This paragraph applies where the chemical manufacturer, importer, or distributor can demonstrate that it is not feasible to use pull-out labels, fold-back labels, or tags containing the full label information required by paragraph (f)(1)"; (f)(12)(ii): "For a container less than or equal to 100 ml capacity, the chemical manufacturer, importer, or distributor must include, at a minimum, the following information on the label of the container: (A) Product identifier; (B) Pictogram(s); (C) Signal word; (D) Chemical manufacturer's name and phone number; and (E) A statement that the full label information for the hazardous chemical is provided on the immediate outer package."
No minimum pictogram size exists anywhere in 1910.1200 (no "cm"/"mm" figure for pictograms); (f)(1)(iv) reads only "Pictogram(s);" and C.2.3.1 sets only shape and colour.

answers.notes: Bottom line: "Add precautionary statements to be fully compliant" — implies nothing else is missing; misses the phone number.
